title: Automated Mass Spectrum Labelling in Atom Probe Tomography
content: Quantitative concentration analysis in atom probe tomography [1] (APT) relies on peak ranging and labeling in time-of-flight spectra or converted mass-to-charge-ratio (m/z) spectra. This is primarily a manual process, which can limit reproducibility and objectivity, and is subject to data complexities including varying noise level, m/z resolution, peak overlaps, and user subjectivity. Recently, there has been promising progress in developing automatic methods for peak identification. Mikhalychev et al. [2] applied a Bayesian approach that iteratively accepts top-ranked ions according to their calculated posterior probabilities, while taking into account prior information. Wei et al. [3] introduced a supervised machine learning method that leverages natural isotopic abundance patterns to identify elemental and molecular peaks through model training. Here, we propose a two-stage, supervised learning approach: first, a ranging model recognizes peaks and determines their boundaries, and second, an ion labeling model identifies each peak with a specific ion species. The ranging model enables automatic peak ranging for APT m/z spectra with objectivity across different sample materials and varying data quality . The ion labeling model assigns a primary element label for each peak and provides a confidence score to flag uncertain predictions.
